title: Accessible E-commerce Checkout Validation
business: A boutique online retailer managing a complex checkout flow.
problem: Frequent UI refactors break brittle tests that rely on internal component state and CSS selectors, leading to high maintenance costs and false negatives.
solution: By utilizing DOM Testing Library, the team shifts focus to user-centric queries like getByRole and getByLabelText, ensuring tests remain stable even when the underlying component structure changes.
steps: Identify elements by their semantic role such as button or heading to ensure accessibility compliance.
Use user-event libraries to simulate realistic interactions like typing or clicking instead of triggering internal methods.
Assert the presence of visible text or state changes that a real user would perceive on the screen.
Refactor existing tests to remove reliance on internal component state or private methods.
outcome: The test suite becomes resilient to structural refactoring, allowing developers to update component internals without breaking the verification of core checkout functionality.
limitation: Testing Library focuses on DOM-based interactions, meaning it cannot easily verify non-visual side effects or complex internal logic that does not manifest in the DOM; check this by verifying if the test can pass while the underlying business logic is completely broken.
